activities.desc: Depart from Pittsburgh (PIT) or Morgantown (MGW). EDT → CEST (+6h). Shortest routes usually connect via Reykjavik or London. Families can be on same or separate flights
Stroll the harbor promenade with shops, restaurants, and marina views. Great jet-lag walk
Munch's The Scream, Viking gold, and Norwegian art. Indoor, central, jet-lag-friendly - located right by Aker Brygge and City Hall
Walk the sloping marble roof for iconic city + fjord views. The architecture alone is worth it
200+ granite and bronze sculptures by Gustav Vigeland in Frogner Park. Oslo's top free attraction

activities.text: Karl Johans Gate & Royal Palace Walk
activities.desc: Oslo's main boulevard from Central Station to the Royal Palace. Street musicians, cafes, shops
Viking artifacts, medieval church art, Miðgarðr Viking exhibition.
Modern art scattered through forest trails with panoramic Oslo Fjord views. Quieter than Vigeland
Guided craft beer tour through Grünerløkka with 3-4 brewery stops and tastings included. Age limit 18. Book ahead
Indoor food market at Vulkan with Norwegian specialties, international stalls, and the Hopyard craft beer bar. Great for dinner
15 min metro + 20 min hike. The local sunset spot with panoramic Oslofjord views from a rocky ridge. Far less crowded than Holmenkollen. Bring a blanket and thermos
20 min bus #56. Restaurant with a free viewpoint above it. Golden hour fjord views that stretch forever in late May
Michelin Bib Gourmand in St. Hanshaugen. Family-style sharing plates rooted in Norwegian terroir. The Sunday roast concept is a local institution. Reserve ahead
Centrally located in Sentrum near the Palace Park. Cozy, sustainable restaurant serving excellent traditional Norwegian comfort food like reindeer stew and local fish soup
22 house and guest taps of great Norwegian-style IPAs, sours, and solid porters. Hearty English pub and European rustic food menu. Back room has board games

25 taps of Norwegian microbrews in a renovated mechanics workshop near the bus station. Laid back and cozy. Note: No food menu, but you are welcome to bring outside food or order delivery straight to your table!
Located in Grünerløkka. World-famous barista and coffee roaster. Single-origin espresso and filter only. No WiFi, no laptops. The real deal
Near the Palace Park. Vintage 1950s interior with mid-century furniture. Pour-over by day, award-winning cocktail bar at night. Hidden back courtyard oasis
Sweat out the jet lag in a waterfront urban sauna, then take a refreshing plunge directly into the cold Oslofjord. Ultimate internal-clock reset. Book 2 weeks ahead
Take the B1 public ferry from City Hall Pier 4. A 7-min ride brings you to peaceful trails, 12th-century monastery ruins, and rocky beaches. Low physical effort
Located on Bygdøy peninsula. Built entirely around the massive 1892 polar exploration ship Fram. Highly visual and interactive, great when mentally foggy
Atmospheric brewpub in a historic, rustic 100-year-old brick cellar in Grünerløkka. Excellent house-brewed beers and open fireplace to fight evening fatigue
Warm, unpretentious tavern specializing in slow-cooked pork. Famous for their incredible, tender roasted pork knuckle (svineknoke) and local microbrews
Eccentric bohemian tavern near Palace Park operating since the 1870s. Packed with antiques and taxidermy. Massive list of 200+ beers and classic Scandinavian fare
Dimly lit maritime-themed tavern at Youngstorget square. Intimate environment serving arguably the best comfort-food burgers in the city and a huge aquavit list
Cozy local neighborhood gem hidden away in historic Kampen. Offers a simple, rustic 2-to-3-course chalkboard menu that updates daily using ultra-fresh ingredients
Classic 19th-century "brown cafe" in St. Hanshaugen with wood booths and old-school vibes. Known for traditional home-cooked Norwegian kjøttkaker (meatballs)
Seaside restaurant built out like a rustic timber fisherman's cabin. Offers a large open fireplace and traditional coastal Arctic stews, fish soups, and venison
Bustling, comforting traditional Italian trattoria in a beautiful brick building at Schous plass. Renowned for spectacular fresh, house-made oxtail ragu ravioli
Modern diner with comfortable leather booths and low ambient lighting right next to Mathallen. Premium gourmet burgers, thick microbrews, and spiked milkshakes
Tiny, artisanal one-man bakery along the river in Lilliborg. The premier spot for a classic Norwegian BMO (sourdough roll with thick butter and caramelized brown cheese)
Informal, art-filled all-day spot in Sentrum. Go early for an authentic Scandi breakfast of boiled eggs, artisanal cheese, warm bread, berries, and premium filter coffee
Warm neighborhood cafe in upper Grünerløkka known for its relaxed vibes, exceptional sourdough bakes, and signature thick "fat pancakes" with seasonal compote
Peaceful, historic bakery hidden in a quiet courtyard behind the Palace Park. Outstanding traditional Norwegian skoleboller and artisan hand-laminated pastries

groupNotes: Keep Day 1 light - see Jet Lag Playbook. National Museum (The Scream) and the Opera House roof walk are central and easy-paced. Vigeland Park is a lovely open-air option. For sunset, take the metro to Vettakollen for panoramic fjord views.

meals.breakfast: Included hotel buffet or Godt Brød - skolebrød (custard bun), kanelboller, open-faced sandwiches
meals.lunch: Mathallen Oslo food hall (Vulkan) - seafood soup at Vulkanfisk, tacos, Asian street food. Or grab smørbrød at a local bakery
meals.dinner: Den Glade Gris - Norwegian pork-focused gastropub (try ribbe or nakkekoteletter). Or RIB for slow-cooked beef ribs. After dinner, walk to Himkok for a craft aquavit cocktail or Schouskjelleren for a nightcap

directions: Take E16 and Rv7 northwest from Oslo through Hønefoss.
Turn onto Rv52 at Gol, passing through Hemsedal valley and the mountain pass.
Merge onto E16 near Borlo, passing Borgund Stave Church and Lærdal Town.
Pass through Lærdalstunnelen directly into Aurland/Flåm region.

stops.desc: Scenic waterfall right off E16 near Hønefoss

stops.name: Rjukandefossen Waterfall
stops.desc: Powerful double waterfall roadside stop in Hemsedal along Rv52

stops.name: Borgund Stave Church
stops.desc: Best preserved stave church, built 1150. Guided tours available

stops.name: Midtødegården Cheese Farm
stops.desc: Traditional Norwegian goat cheese farm near Borgund

stops.name: Lærdal Town
stops.desc: Charming village before the tunnel entrance - historic Old Lærdalsøyri wooden houses

stops.name: Lærdalstunnelen
stops.desc: World's longest road tunnel (24.5 km). Blue light caves split the driving segments

stops.name: Aurland Shoe Factory
stops.desc: Historic shoe factory turned visitor storefront right before arriving in Flåm

groupNotes: Drive in separate cars. Order of scenic stops mapped accurately sequentially: Hønefoss -> Norefjell -> Rjukandefossen -> Borgund -> Lærdal Town -> Tunnel -> Aurland -> Flåm.

meals.lunch: Car picnic with bread, local Norvegia cheese, and snacks from an Oslo grocery stop.
meals.dinner: Flåm Marina Restaurant - seafood with Aurlandsfjord views. Grilled salmon or fresh fish soup.

activities.desc: Guided stillwater kayak departing from Flåm beach beachfront outfitter base.
Flåm–Myrdal, 867m elevation gain. Stops at Kjosfossen waterfall.
Wooden viewing platform 650m above Aurlandsfjord. Winding road ascent from Aurland.
Short steep hike up to a waterfall viewpoint overlooking Flåm valley.

groupNotes: Morning: take the Flåm Railway. Afternoon: Drive up to Stegastein viewpoint and add the Brekkefossen hike later in the afternoon.

directions: Take E16 west from Flåm through Flenjatunnelen and Gudvangatunnelen toward Voss.
Stop at Voss Rafting Center along the Raundalselva river system.
Continue west on E16 past Tvindefossen directly into Bergen center.
Fantoft Disc Golf course is located 10 minutes south of Bergen core.

stops.name: Stalheim Viewpoint
stops.desc: Historic panoramic drop viewpoint overlooking the Nærøydalen canyon right off E16 route.

stops.name: Tvindefossen Waterfall
stops.desc: Beautiful multi-tiered roadside waterfall near Voss. Easy access photo point off E16

activities.desc: Class 2-3 rapids on Raundalselva. Equipment and guides provided.
Wooded technical layout located next to Fantoft Stave Church south of Bergen.
Explore the historic Hanseatic timber waterfront lines under extended twilight.

groupNotes: Do not take the Lærdal tunnel or Snow road today; head straight west towards Voss. Fantoft features both the historic stave church reconstruction and the 18-hole disc golf park closely paired together.

activities.desc: Cable car ride for panoramic harbor framing. Trail links up high.
Outdoor harbor stalls alongside indoor seafood pavilions.
Learn architectural and merchant histories across the ancient wood frames.
Bergen's highest peak access for 360 sweeping ridge views.

meals.dinner: Bare Vestland or Pingvinen - cozy neighborhood pubs emphasizing raspeballer or locally sourced classic components.

directions: Take Rv7/E16 east from Bergen toward Trengereid.
Follow Rv7 past Norheimsund to Steinsdalsfossen waterfall.
Track Rv7 east hugging the fjord coast, crossing the spans of the Hardanger Bridge.
Arrive in Eidfjord valley at water level, then ascend Måbødalen canyon to Vøringsfossen.

stops.name: Steinsdalsfossen Waterfall
stops.desc: Famous waterfall featuring an accessible structural concrete pathway built BEHIND the flow cascade.

stops.name: Hardanger Bridge Lookout
stops.desc: Scenic overlook point framing one of the longest suspension designs globally.

stops.name: Vøringsfossen Waterfall
stops.desc: Massive 182m waterfall drop. Modern architectural cantilever steps map over the cliff edges above Eidfjord town.

groupNotes: Drive to Eidfjord first at sea level before ascending the interior road tracks to find Vøringsfossen. Bondhusbreen glacier is skipped today and placed cleanly into Day 7 routing to avoid major detours.

directions: Drive south from Ulvik/Odda down through valley corridor Rv13.
Join E134 west, tracing along the banks of Åkrafjorden.
Pass Langfossen waterfall, then continue west directly through Aksdal junction.
Take E39 south to Mortavika terminal, catch the Mortavika–Arsvågen vehicle ferry, then follow E39 south directly into Stavanger center.
